extracted.intended_audience: Applicants seeking admission to the USPTO registration (patent) examination (patent agent/attorney applicants), including former USPTO employees seeking waivers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for demonstrating scientific/technical training, eligibility, application completion, fees, testing procedures, and post-exam requirements to obtain registration to practice in patent matters before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A: Degree in a Recognized Technical Subject
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is considered to possess necessary scientific and technical training if they provide an official transcript showing that a bachelor's, master’s, or Ph.D. degree was awarded in one of the listed recognized technical subjects (long enumerated list: e.g., biology, chemistry, physics, various engineering fields, computer science* etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An official transcript is required (diploma or copy not accepted); transcript must include university stamp or seal. The Office will accept degrees showing equivalence to a Category A degree (e.g., molecular cell biology equivalent to biology). For computer science, an acceptable degree must be a Bachelor of Science from an accredited institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Degree in Other Subjects — Equivalence via Coursework or Other Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with a bachelor's, master’s or Ph.D. in a subject not listed in Category A must establish to the OED Director that they possess scientific and technical training equivalent to a Category A degree by satisfying one of Options 1–4, other training, or other education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit objective evidence and necessary documentation (official transcripts, course descriptions, etc.) showing satisfaction of the chosen option or other means of qualifying. Burden of proof is on applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B Option 1: 24 semester hours in physics
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfy Category B by completing 24 semester hours in physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only physics courses for physics majors will be accepted. Official transcripts required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B Option 2: 32 semester hours (chemistry/physics + biology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfy Category B by completing 32 semester hours consisting of eight semester hours in a combination of chemistry or physics (with at least one lab) and 24 semester hours in biology, botany, microbiology, or molecular biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only courses for science or engineering majors will be accepted. Official transcripts and concurrent course descriptions required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B Option 3: 30 semester hours in chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfy Category B by completing 30 semester hours in chemistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only chemistry courses for chemistry majors will be accepted. Official transcripts required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B Option 4: 40 semester hours mixed science/engineering coursework
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfy Category B by completing 40 semester hours consisting of eight semester hours in a combination of chemistry, physics, or biology (with at least one lab) and 32 semester hours in chemistry, physics, biology, botany, microbiology, molecular biology, or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All acceptable coursework for Options 2 and 4 must be for science or engineering majors. Course descriptions concurrent with the year taken are required. Up to four semester hours in design engineering or drafting accepted under Option 4; certain rigorous computer science courses (theory/analysis/design with lab/software development) can count but may not substitute for the 8-semester-hour chemistry/physics requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Transcripts and Course Descriptions Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Official transcripts must be provided to establish both the award of degrees and completion of each course relied upon for Category B qualifications. For each course relied upon, furnish an official course description concurrent with the year the course was taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcripts must be official and include university stamp/seal. A transcript issued to an applicant will be accepted if stamped/sealed. A diploma, copy of diploma, or letter from registrar is insufficient. Course descriptions must include catalog cover page/year, major requirements, and complete pages describing courses. Highlight courses on transcripts to speed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Minimum Grade Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only courses with a grade of C- or better will be accepted for establishing Category B coursework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should highlight acceptable courses on transcripts and include course descriptions to demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Quarter/Trimester to Semester Hour Conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Credits earned in quarters or trimesters must be converted to semester hours by multiplying quarter or trimester hours by 2/3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must adjust credits from institutions with terms shorter than a typical 15–18 week semester to determine satisfaction of Category B requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Translations for Foreign Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified English translations of foreign-language documents (transcripts, course descriptions, other supporting documentation) must be furnished for those documents to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must be certified; foreign education must include objective evidence of equivalence (see Other Education).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Other Acceptable Course Work (Computer Science and Design Courses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Option 4, up to four semester hours accepted for design engineering/drafting. Certain computer science courses that stress theoretical foundations, analysis, and design with substantial laboratory work (including software development) will be accepted (examples listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable CS topics include representation/transformation of information structures, algorithms, data structures, programming languages with lab, computer organization and architecture, AI/robotics, networking, linear/logic circuits, operating systems, software methodology/engineering. Such CS courses may not substitute for the eight semester hours of chemistry or physics required under Option 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B: Typical Non-Acceptable Course Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses that typically do not demonstrate required scientific and technical training are listed (e.g., anthropology; audited courses; behavioral science; CLE; management; computer software use courses; vocational training; high school level courses; mathematics; patent law courses; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also not accepted: correspondence courses; courses for non-science majors; courses taken pass/fail; corporate or one-day conference training; college research or seminar courses without set content; courses that repeat or are lesser-included than already-credited courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B/C/D: Other Training and Other Education Equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: Other education (foreign education, academic credit for work experience, military education, life experience, CLEP credits, institutionally granted life-experience credits) may be acceptable to the extent objective evidence demonstrates equivalence to a Category A subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable showings: accredited U.S. college accepts specific courses for college credit in Category A subject; CLEP credits accepted by accredited institution; life experience for which the institution identified course areas in Category A; foreign education evaluated by private organizations that deem it equivalent; credits from certain federal graduate schools if accepted by accredited institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category C: Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) Test Option
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant relying on practical engineering or scientific experience may qualify by taking and passing the FE test (developed/administered by state engineering boards). Official FE test results and an official bachelor's transcript must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FE is administered by state boards (not USPTO). Applicant should contact appropriate State Board secretaries for FE test administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D: Design Patent Practice Only (Degrees in Recognized Design Subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant will be considered to have necessary training for design patent practice if they provide an official transcript showing a bachelor's, master’s, or Ph.D. degree in a recognized design subject (e.g., architecture, applied arts, fine/studio arts, graphic design, industrial design, product design, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant registered under Category D may practice only in design patent matters. Official transcript requirements are the same as Category A (diploma or copy not accepted; transcript must show equivalence if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: All Business Transacted in Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: All business with the USPTO should be transacted in writing; actions of OED regarding an application will be based exclusively on the written record in the Office (see 37 CFR § 1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal attendance is unnecessary; applicants must maintain and update written records as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of Aliens and Limited Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-U.S. citizens who do not reside in the U.S. are not eligible for registration except under 37 CFR § 11.6(c) (reciprocity). Limited recognition and conditions for aliens and lawful permanent residents are governed by 37 CFR § 11.9(b); Canadian IP Office currently recognized for substantial reciprocity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aliens must provide documentation showing authorization to reside and work/train in the U.S. (copies of immigration documents, both sides of work/training authorizations). Pending approvals result in denial of admission. Qualifying aliens under specified immigration code sections are not 'registered' upon passing but may receive limited recognition under § 11.9(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible Applicants — Convictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'conviction' per 37 CFR § 11.1; applicants convicted of a felony or a crime involving moral turpitude or breach of trust are not eligible to apply for registration during sentence/probation/parole and for two years after successful completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applicants must file fees specified and the OED Director will determine satisfactory proof of reform and rehabilitation; the applicant bears burden and may need to submit fees for each determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible Applicants — Disciplined Professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants disbarred from the practice of law or other professions, or who resigned a professional license in lieu of proceedings, are ineligible to apply for registration for five years from date of disbarment/resignation; applicants suspended on ethical grounds are ineligible until suspension expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If also convicted of disqualifying crimes, both ineligibility conditions apply. Fees required for OED determinations must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible Applicants — Previously Denied for Lack of Good Moral Character
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant refused registration for failure to demonstrate present good moral character and reputation is ineligible to reapply for two years after the decision (unless shortened by USPTO Director). Applicants who withdrew while under investigation are similarly ineligible for two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applicants must pay required fees and have the burden of showing fitness to practice; must retake and pass the registration examination even if previously passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission Requirements and Required Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for admission to the examination, submit a completed Application for Registration (Form PTO-158), applicable fees, official transcripts, course descriptions (Category B), and any other required documentation (e.g., evidence of permanent residence, documents responding to moral character questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply online at the Exam Applicant Portal or by mail to Mailstop OED. Applications must be complete; facsimile transmissions not accepted. Incomplete applications are strongly discouraged. Specific fees and submission instructions provided (see fees rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for Completing Application Form PTO-158
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete form in permanent ink or computer, personally sign as required, provide complete legal name (first, middle, last), provide name as on government-issued photo ID on line 1b, provide daytime address for communications, and report required information (citizenship, DOB, place of birth, visa classification, permanent resident status, alien registration number, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide exact legal name or match ID will result in incomplete application or denial of admission. All changes (including address) must be reported in writing within 30 days and the application must be updated until registered. No changes via phone, fax, or email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification for Examination Admission
rubrics_metrics.description: For admission to the Prometric testing center, bring a current, valid State or Federal government-issued ID containing both photograph and signature. The name on the ID must exactly match line 1b of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single ID suffices. Admission denied if ID is invalid or name mismatch. An admission letter will not be accepted and no name changes permitted at test centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing Administration and Prometric Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration examination is computer-based and administered by Prometric. Prometric provides site locations, a 15-minute tutorial before the exam, a 15-minute survey after the exam, scratch paper and pencil, and schedules/reschedules via web or phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prometric test centers perform signature logs, electronic photographs, and record entry/exit times. Continuous video monitoring and site proctoring are used. If a testing center is unable to deliver exam due to emergency, exam will be rescheduled without charge. Prometric toll-free number and website provided for scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Not to Bring and Test Materials Provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not bring reference materials, study materials, notes, or scratch paper into the testing area. Reference materials are available on the computer delivering the examination. Prometric provides scratch paper and pencil which will be collected and destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No materials permitted other than provided scratch paper. Removing scratch paper is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing Center Protocols: Breaks, Cheating, and Consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an optional timed one-hour lunch break; no other timed breaks are built in (unscheduled breaks continue test timing). Cheating (copying/photographing questions, recording answers elsewhere, bringing notes, leaving to consult notes, etc.) will result in being escorted from the testing area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants found cheating will be removed; Prometric provides continual proctoring and video monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling, Rescheduling, and No-Show Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants schedule/reschedule exams through Prometric online or by phone. Failure to appear for a scheduled exam causes loss of Prometric eligibility and forfeiture of all fees paid to the USPTO; if sufficient time remains in testing period, OED may reset eligibility upon contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If testing center cancels due to technical/emergency, exam will be rescheduled at no charge. Applicants who withdraw/are denied admission must reapply and pay fees again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Failed Examination Questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of the mailing date of results, an unsuccessful applicant may review (but not copy) the questions and answers they answered incorrectly in a review session at a Prometric test site or at OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notes or copies may be taken. Only one review session permitted per examination taken. Review scheduled through Prometric or OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication After Failure to Pass
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsuccessful applicant may reapply to take the examination but must wait 30 days after the date of the last examination before retaking. Eligibility for retesting is controlled by OED; do not contact Prometric about retesting eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reapplicants must submit a new Form PTO-158, $118 nonrefundable application fee, $226 registration examination fee, and any other documentation needed to update the application. Additional fee rules apply for applicants subject to moral character determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund Policy for USPTO Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The $118 application fee is non-refundable. The $226 registration examination fee is non-refundable after OED receives an application except as noted. Registration exam fee refunded only if OED denies admission due to incomplete application or failing to meet qualifications; special refund rules apply for $1,806 fee under 37 CFR § 1.21(a)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant submitted the $1,806 fee and is denied admission, refund will be that fee less the $118 application fee. Fees not paid by mistake or in excess are non-refundable. Applicants withdrawing after admission or failing to appear must file another application and pay fees again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR § 11.3 may be filed requesting that a regulatory requirement (not a statutory requirement) be suspended or waived in extraordinary situations when justice requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should be filed in writing and must show extraordinary circumstances justifying waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful Completion — Moral Character Solicitation and Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon successful completion (or waiver) of the examination, the OED Director will publish a solicitation for information concerning the applicant’s moral character and reputation and will investigate any adverse information before completing registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adverse information is received, an investigation will be conducted after passing/waiver. Applicants must respond to further steps from OED. Passing certificate of examination is valid for two years for completion of registration; otherwise applicant must retake exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Good Standing Requirement for Attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant desiring to be registered as an attorney must submit a certificate of good standing from the bar of the highest court of the State in which they are admitted; the certificate must be less than six months old and should be filed with the Data Sheet (Form PTO 107A) after notice of passing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certificate or letter from the state bar is not acceptable. Do not file certificate of good standing with the application. Attorneys for whom no certificate is received will be registered as a patent agent or design patent agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Mailing Under 37 CFR § 1.8 Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When mailing application materials, include a Certificate of Mailing identifying the correspondence, the mailing date, and signature; each paper must have its own certificate or the certificate must identify each submitted paper and be enclosed in the mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate must be in the envelope with the materials mailed. Applicants are urged to provide institutions sending transcripts with a copy of the certificate of mailing and request inclusion in the transcript envelope.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Privacy Act Advisory — Furnishing Information is Voluntary but Required for Admission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Act advisory provides that furnishing requested data is voluntary, but if information is not furnished, the applicant will not be admitted to the registration examination or registered to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advisory describes routine uses, potential disclosures, and legal authority for collection (35 U.S.C. §§ 1.6 and 31). Applicants should be aware disclosures may be made in certain investigative or litigation contexts.
